step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified the on-premises database actor ('OnPremDC') on the left side sending data to the Storage Gateway.
2. Identified Storage Gateway ('StorageGateway') connecting via Direct Connect ('DirectConnect') to AWS Cloud.
3. Ingested data lands in the S3 Landing bucket ('S3').
4. Processing is driven by Quality Cleansing EC2 instance ('EC2') fetching scripts/metadata from RDS ('RDS') and writing output to the S3 Transformation bucket ('S3').
5. Transformation EC2 instance ('EC2') fetches metadata/scripts from RDS ('RDS'), reads from Transformation S3 bucket, and loads processed data into Redshift ('RedShift').
6. Redshift exports/publishes data to S3 Publish bucket ('S3'), which subsequently transitions aged data to Glacier S3 bucket ('S3').
7. All connections and flow directions are modeled strictly according to physical arrows drawn on the whiteboard.

edges.notes: On-premises database feeds data into AWS Storage Gateway
Storage Gateway transfers daily incremental data over Direct Connect
Direct Connect delivers data to Landing S3 bucket
Quality Cleansing EC2 pulls raw data from Landing S3 bucket
Quality Cleansing EC2 fetches/updates processing metadata with RDS
RDS supplies metadata and transformation scripts to Quality Cleansing EC2
Quality Cleansing EC2 writes output to Transformation S3 bucket
Transformation EC2 reads data from Transformation S3 bucket
Transformation EC2 fetches metadata and scripts from RDS
RDS provides schema/script metadata to Transformation EC2
Transformation EC2 loads facts and dimensions into Redshift
Redshift Spectrum publishes report-ready data directly to Publish S3 bucket
Aged publish data transitioned to Glacier S3 bucket via retention lifecycle rule
